links.outcome: Perceived protocol quality: novice with AI vs AI alone vs expert, blinded ratings
links.effect: EP scored highest, NAI intermediate, AI alone lowest across all five conditions (e.g., scoliosis 4.35/3.96/3.38; Friedman p<0.001); NAI vs AI significant except osteoporosis (p=0.362).
links.quote: Across all investigated pathologies, the APA protocols designed by the EP consistently achieved the highest overall evaluation scores, followed by the protocols developed by the NAI, while the AI protocols received the lowest scores.

links.outcome: Comparison of AI-generated protocols against expert clinician protocols on same prescriptions
links.effect: Expert protocols rated significantly higher than AI-alone in all conditions (EP vs AI p<0.01), notably safety, tailoring and progression.
links.quote: Post hoc analyses showed that EP protocols received significantly higher rating than AI protocols in all conditions (p < 0.01).

links.outcome: Quality of autonomous AI exercise protocols versus expert-led protocols, informing need for clinician authority
links.effect: AI-alone protocols consistently lowest rated (all p<0.05); authors conclude AI without human oversight is not suitable for autonomous prescription.
links.quote: AI-generated protocols without human oversight are not yet suitable for autonomous APA prescription, supporting a complementary, expertise-dependent role of AI in exercise programming.

links.outcome: Perceived safety and appropriateness of AI-alone exercise protocols vs experts
links.effect: AI-alone protocols scored lower on safety (e.g., scoliosis safe 3.6 vs 4.54 EP; osteoarthritis 3.52 vs 4.64); EP-AI differences most pronounced for safety (p<0.01).
links.quote: Differences between EP and AI were most pronounced for safety (p < 0.01), appropriateness (tailoring p < 0.01), and progression (p < 0.05), whereas EP-NAI differences were smaller and condition-dependent.

links.outcome: Quality of output from human-AI team (novice+AI) versus AI alone and expert
links.effect: Novice with AI support scored intermediate, partially closing the expertise gap; NAI higher than AI alone in most conditions (p<0.01) but not equal to EP.
links.quote: NAI protocols showed intermediate performance, partially reducing the expertise gap.
